articles.title: From the Editor’s Desk: A New Beginning in the Journey of Medical Science
articles.abstract: Welcome message to the inaugural issue of the JMN Journal of Medical Sciences, the official academic publication of JMN Medical College. Outlining the institutional commitment to enquiry, scholarship, ethical practice, and responsible sharing of medical knowledge.

articles.title: A Study on Urinary Incontinence and Its Risk Factors Among Post-menopausal Women in a Rural Area of West Bengal
articles.abstract: Background: Urinary incontinence (UI) is the involuntary loss of urine which is objectively demonstrable and is a social and hygienic problem. Objectives: To find out the proportion of rural post-menopausal women having UI and its associated risk factors. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted in a rural area of Barasat among 120 elderly women (≥50 years) selected by cluster sampling. Results: 43 (35.8%) of 120 women were found to have UI. The most prevalent type was stress UI (18.3%), followed by mixed UI (10.8%) and urge UI (5.8%). On multivariable analysis, illiteracy, parity >3, history of gynaecological operation, chronic cough, and LUTS remained significantly associated. Conclusion: Rural women are at high risk of developing UI, and awareness generation is needed.

articles.title: A Study on Assessment of Functional Status and Its Correlates Among the Geriatric Population in Rural India
articles.abstract: Background: Functional ability is a proxy for healthy aging and is related not only to mental and physical health but also to social well-being. Objectives: To determine the magnitude of poor functional status among the geriatric population and its correlates. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 246 geriatric people in a rural area of West Bengal. Results: 32.5% and 59.3% of participants were dependent for basic ADL and IADL, respectively. Age >70 years, female gender, less education, widowed status, joint family, poorest economic status, depression, and multimorbidity were associated with increased dependency. Conclusion: Community-based comprehensive geriatric health and disability assessment should be provided.

articles.title: Management of Mesiodens: A Supernumerary Tooth
articles.abstract: Supernumerary tooth is a developmental disturbance associated with the number of teeth. Mesiodens is a supernumerary tooth present in the midline between the two central incisors. It usually results in oral problems such as malocclusion, food impaction, and poor aesthetics. This case report deals with the management of a palatally placed, fully erupted mesiodens in the maxillary arch of a 7-year-old male patient, extracted under local anaesthesia following radiographic confirmation.

articles.title: Scrub Typhus Presenting as Severe Pneumonia and Acute Febrile Illness in a Malnourished Infant with Infantile Tremor Syndrome
articles.abstract: Background: Scrub typhus is an important cause of acute undifferentiated febrile illness in endemic regions of India. Clinical Description: A 6-month-old male infant presented with fever for 10 days, cough and respiratory distress for 4 days, and features of infantile tremor syndrome. Scrub typhus IgM was reactive. Management & Outcome: Treated with intravenous antibiotics, doxycycline, and parenteral vitamin B12 with rapid clinical improvement. Conclusion: Scrub typhus should be considered in infants presenting with prolonged fever and pneumonia in endemic areas.

articles.title: Vestibulo-Cerebellar Modulation of Stress-Related Immune Responses: A Narrative Review
articles.abstract: The vestibulo-cerebellum occupies a distinctive anatomical position with connections to the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, sympathetic-adrenomedullary (SAM) system, and locus coeruleus. This narrative review summarizes literature examining whether vestibular and vestibulo-cerebellar stimulation can modulate stress-induced immune alterations, discussing neuroendocrine pathways, GABAergic modulation, and preclinical evidence.
